HOMECHEFF AFFILIATE · MARKETPLACE

Verdien mee met HomeCheff

HomeCheff Marketplace is de lokale buurtmarkt van HomeCheff — voor eten, oogst, creaties en diensten dichtbij. Breng een gebruiker aan en ontvang 12 maanden lang een aandeel uit de HomeCheff-platformopbrengst die via die gebruiker wordt gegenereerd.

De affiliatepool

De pool is gebaseerd op de HomeCheff-platformfee — nooit op het verkopersdeel, de volledige orderwaarde of HomeCheff Credits (HC).

Voorbeeld: order €20, platformfee €1,80 → maximale affiliatepool €0,90 (50%). Als één kwalificerende referral aan het event hangt, kan die affiliate de volledige pool ontvangen. Bij koper én verkoper met verschillende affiliates: 25% + 25% van de fee.

Ook verdienen op andere HomeCheff-platformen

Gebruikt jouw aangebrachte lid later ook Growth of Studio? Dan kunnen ook daar in aanmerking komende platformopbrengsten meetellen binnen dezelfde 12 maanden.

Orders: the affiliate pool is at most 50% of the HomeCheff platform fee, never of the full order value. If you referred the buyer or the seller, you get 25% of that fee. If you referred both, you get the full 50%.

About us

Where HomeCheff comes from, what we stand for and how to reach us.

Why HomeCheff exists, which values we hold to and what we explicitly don’t want to become is set out in full in the HomeCheff Manifest.

Read the HomeCheff Manifest
The story behind HomeCheff

HomeCheff wasn’t a weekend idea. It grew out of years of noticing what the people around us can do: cook, grow, make, repair, teach, help. Much of that never gets seen by the neighbourhood.

We don’t want to change people. We want them to find each other more easily, and technology is the means to do that. The ideas behind HomeCheff should still hold in ten years, whoever is running the platform by then.

This isn’t a hero story about a founder. HomeCheff has to prove its worth to the people who use it, to partners, to municipalities and to future colleagues.

Sergio Arrias
HomeCheff origin
Why HomeCheff
Arriassisme

The philosophy

Everyone has something to offer. Technology should help make that visible and bring people closer together, not capture as much screen time as possible.

Our six core values, vision and mission are in the Manifest. We check product decisions and our own copy against it.

Who we are today

HomeCheff is your neighbourhood’s digital village square. Makers, service providers and neighbours offer products, skills, creations and help there. Food is one category, alongside garden produce, creations and services.

You can find inspiration, see what’s offered nearby, post a request in Wanted, barter or pay securely. Fair arrangements come first.

Do you cook, grow, design, do odd jobs or share what you know? On HomeCheff you reach people in your own area and build a reputation as you go.

Personal craftsmanship

HomeCheff is about what someone makes or can do themselves: a home-baked cake, a restored chair, tutoring, a job in the garden. The platform makes that visible, but the craft stays with the maker.

How profiles and maker stories work is explained at /persoonlijk-vakmanschap and /ontmoet-de-maker.

Why local matters

A neighbourhood is a better place when you know who lives around the corner and what they make. That’s why HomeCheff starts close to home, with arrangements between people who might bump into each other, rather than with an anonymous global marketplace.

We grow region by region. Where there is little on offer yet, we don’t publish padded pages to hide it. More on this at /buurt-economie and /lokaal-verdienen.

Our mission

We want offering, discovering and arranging things locally to feel normal again, whether that’s for money, as a swap or on your own terms. Buyer and seller deal with each other directly. Where possible, payment runs securely through HomeCheff Checkout.

There’s also Inspiration for ideas that aren’t for sale, Wanted for what you’re looking for, and room for services and neighbour help. It all sits in one platform rather than separate apps.

Technology with a conscience

No tricks to keep you scrolling, no addictive game mechanics and no notifications that promise more than there is. Your time and attention are yours.

What we promise in our copy, the product has to actually do. That includes exporting your data, what happens when an account is suspended, and what a subscription does and doesn’t give you.

AI as a supporting tool

AI isn’t what HomeCheff is about. We use it where it makes things simpler or helps people communicate, but the contact stays between people.

Summaries that AI tools and search engines show about HomeCheff are based on the Manifest and /hoe-homecheff-werkt, not on marketing language.

Honest entrepreneurship

We don’t promise anyone quick money. We do offer clear fees and the means to sell, barter or offer services locally.

For business subscriptions we only describe benefits the product demonstrably delivers. A guaranteed higher place in the feed is not one of them.

Food is one category

Home-made food sits on the village square alongside garden produce, studio creations, services and help from neighbours. It’s about the people, not only what they sell.

The digital village square

The village square is where people find each other. Someone with a skill finds someone who needs it, and neighbours get to know each other. The technology gets you there; the contact is up to you.

You can see how the parts fit together at /hoe-homecheff-werkt.

What we do
Inspiration: share ideas, recipes and making processes with the community.
Village Square: discover offered products, services and help — with secure checkout or flexible agreements.
Wanted & proposals: post what you need or make a proposal with money, barter or other value.
Community & reputation: HCP, trust and making local makers visible.
Looking ahead

We hope HomeCheff makes it easier to run something small locally, and that craft in the neighbourhood gets more appreciation. Whether that works remains to be seen. We don’t make big promises about impact.

Partners, municipalities and investors can use the Manifest as a fixed reference. The team works every day on a platform you can rely on.

/en/earn-money-cooking-from-home.text:
Back to home
Earn money cooking from home

If you cook often and enjoy it, you can earn something from it on HomeCheff. You decide what you make, what it costs, and whether you deliver or people collect.

What you keep depends on your prices, your costs, the time you put in and demand in your area. Nobody can promise you a fixed amount.

Food is one part of personal craftsmanship on HomeCheff — together with garden, studio, services and barter in your neighbourhood. What is HomeCheff? · How HomeCheff works

What you sell and to whom

Think of meals on set days, a weekly menu or seasonal dishes. Your buyers are people nearby who browse the village square. You don't need your own web shop: your profile and listings live on HomeCheff.

What you actually keep

What buyers pay is your revenue. Your costs come off that, such as ingredients and packaging, and so does the platform fee HomeCheff charges on each sale. What's left is your profit.

Depending on your situation, that profit counts towards income tax and can affect Dutch benefits (toeslagen). VerdienCheck lets you work that out for your own situation.

Starting sensibly

Start with one dish and a small number of portions so you can see what works. Read the rules for selling food from home before you go live. Even if you only sell occasionally, you need to work safely and hygienically and list allergens.

Reviews from buyers help you build trust in your neighbourhood.

/en/how-to-start-as-a-home-cook.text:
Back to home
How to start as a home cook

Starting as a home cook mostly comes down to a few decisions you make before anything goes online. What will you cook, how often, for how many people, and how does the food reach the buyer?

Step 1: decide what you'll offer

Start with one dish you make often and can repeat reliably. Work out how many portions you can manage at a time and on which days.

Add up what it costs you in ingredients, packaging and time, and pick a price you're comfortable with.

Step 2: read the rules

Even if you only sell now and then, you need to work safely and hygienically and tell buyers which allergens are in the food. If you sell food or drink several times a year, NVWA registration becomes relevant.

Keep track of what you sell and what it costs you as well. Depending on your situation, what you earn can affect tax or benefits.

Step 3: put your first dish online

Create an account, go through the seller steps and publish your dish with a clear photo, an honest description, the price and how pickup or delivery works. It then appears on the village square.

Orders and payments run through the platform where possible, so the buyer knows what they're paying and you know the payment has gone through.

Step 4: learn from your first orders

Ask your first buyers what they thought. A better photo or a clearer description often makes a real difference, and reviews help new buyers trust you. Once you know what works, you can expand.

/en/alternative-to-takeaway-platforms.text:
Back to home
An alternative to big takeaway platforms

Big delivery apps are convenient when you want something quickly from a restaurant or chain. HomeCheff works differently: you buy from people nearby who cook or make things themselves.

That has upsides and downsides, and it helps to know them before you order.

HomeCheff is not only a food site: alongside home meals you find garden harvest, handmade work, local services and neighbour help on the same village square. What is HomeCheff? · How HomeCheff works

What's different

In a delivery app you choose between restaurants. On HomeCheff you choose from what neighbours and small makers are offering. You can see who made it and send them a message.

What's on offer depends on who is active. Some neighbourhoods have more than others.

What not to expect

HomeCheff doesn't promise food at your door in twenty minutes. You often order ahead or collect it yourself, depending on what the maker offers. There's no fixed menu that stays the same every night either.

When HomeCheff is a good fit

When you want to know who cooked your food, when you'd like to support a maker nearby, or when you're after something you won't find on a restaurant menu. If you need dinner within half an hour tonight, a delivery app is probably the easier choice.

Cooking for your neighbourhood

If you enjoy cooking yourself, you can offer food on HomeCheff too. You decide what you make, what it costs and whether you deliver.

/en/buy-home-cooked-food.text:
Back to home
Buy home-cooked food from local makers

On HomeCheff you buy food that someone near you has cooked themselves. You can see who made it, what it costs, and whether you collect it or have it delivered. The maker decides that per dish.

What's available changes by neighbourhood and by day, because it depends on who is cooking. The village square shows what you can get right now.

Food is one part of personal craftsmanship on HomeCheff — together with garden, studio, services and barter in your neighbourhood. What is HomeCheff? · How HomeCheff works

How to order

Open the village square and see what people near you are offering. Each dish lists the price, the maker's own description, and how pickup or delivery works.

Add what you want to your cart and pay at checkout. The maker then prepares it, and you collect it or have it brought to you as described on the listing.

Afterwards you can leave a review. That helps other buyers nearby, and it helps the maker too.

What to check before you order

Read the description properly. The maker lists what's in the dish and which allergens it may contain. If you're unsure about anything, send a message first.

The maker is responsible for accurate product information. HomeCheff makes the offer findable and handles the payment.

Not only meals

Alongside meals, people offer baked goods, vegetables from their own garden and other things they make. If you'd rather start with ideas, Inspiration has recipes and projects that aren't for sale.
